units.text: INT. GHOSTS - CONTINUOUS
There is Mrs. Alving's glass, Mr. Alving.
units.name: REGINA

units.text: Yes, but bring one for yourself, Regina.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: REGINA starts and gives a lightning-like side glance at MRS. ALVING.
Why do you wait?
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Softly and hesitatingly.
Is it Mrs. Alving's wish?
units.name: REGINA

units.text: Bring the glass, Regina.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: REGINA goes out into the dining-room.
Follows her with his eyes.
Have you noticed how she walks?--so firmly and lightly!
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: This can never be, Oswald!
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: It's a settled thing. Can't you see that? It's no use saying anything against it.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: REGINA enters with an empty glass, which she keeps in her hand.
Sit down, Regina.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: REGINA looks inquiringly at MRS. ALVING.
Sit down.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: REGINA sits on a chair by the dining room door, still holding the empty glass in her hand.
Oswald--what were you saying about the joy of life?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Ah, the joy of life, mother--that's a thing you don't know much about in these parts. I have never felt it here.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Not when you are with me?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Not when I'm at home. But you don't understand that.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Yes, yes; I think I almost understand it--now.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: And then, too, the joy of work! At bottom, it's the same thing. But that, too, you know nothing about.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Perhaps you are right. Tell me more about it, Oswald.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: I only mean that here people are brought up to believe that work is a curse and a punishment for sin, and that life is something miserable, something it would be best to have done with, the sooner the better.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: "A vale of tears," yes; and we certainly do our best to make it one.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: But in the great world people won't hear of such things. There, nobody really believes such doctrines any longer. There, you feel it a positive bliss and ecstasy merely to draw the breath of life. Mother, have you noticed that everything I have painted has turned upon the joy of life?--always, always upon the joy of life?--light and sunshine and glorious air and faces radiant with happiness. That is why I'm afraid of remaining at home with you.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Afraid? What are you afraid of here, with me?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: I'm afraid lest all my instincts should be warped into ugliness.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Looks steadily at him.
Do you think that is what would happen?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: I know it. You may live the same life here as there, and yet it won't be the same life.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Who has been listening eagerly, rises, her eyes big with thought, and says:.
Now I see the sequence of things.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: What is it you see?
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: I see it now for the first time. And now I can speak.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Rising.
Mother, I don't understand you.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Who has also risen.
Perhaps I ought to go?
units.name: REGINA

units.text: No. Stay here. Now I can speak. Now, my boy, you shall know the whole truth. And then you can choose. Oswald! Regina!
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Hush! The Pastor--
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Enters by the hall door.
There! We have had a most edifying time down there.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: So have we.
units.name: OSWALD
